name: Ion Stoica
title: Professor of Computer Science, UC Berkeley (Xu Bao Chancellor's Chair)
affiliation: UC Berkeley, Director of SkyLab; Co-founder of Databricks, Anyscale, Conviva

notable_papers.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention (vLLM)
notable_papers.contribution: OS-style virtual memory paging for KV cache. 2-4x throughput improvement.

notable_papers.title: SGLang: Efficient Execution of Structured Language Model Programs
notable_papers.contribution: Server-side DSL + JIT for LLM programs. RadixAttention for shared-prefix dedup. Up to 6.4x throughput.

notable_papers.title: RouteLLM: Learning to Route LLMs with Preference Data
notable_papers.contribution: Cost-quality optimization by routing queries to appropriate models using preference-trained classifiers.

notable_papers.title: Chatbot Arena: An Open Platform for Evaluating LLMs by Human Preference
notable_papers.contribution: Crowdsourced pairwise LLM evaluation with Elo ratings. 240K+ votes. De facto LLM leaderboard.

notable_papers.title: BlendServe: Optimizing Offline Inference with Resource-Aware Batching
notable_papers.contribution: Resource-aware batching for offline inference workloads.

research_themes: Systems-first thinking: starts from concrete bottleneck, builds system to solve it
OS/distributed systems analogies applied to ML infrastructure
Empirical evaluation via crowdsourcing over static benchmarks
Full-stack integration: co-design language, compiler, and runtime
Cost-aware design: RouteLLM optimizes cost-quality Pareto frontier
review_critiques: Where are the systems baselines? Demands comparison against vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, TGI -- not toy baselines
This doesn't scale: expects tensor/pipeline parallelism or multi-node awareness
What's the memory footprint? GPU memory is his obsession -- fragmentation, KV cache management
Show me real workloads: suspicious of synthetic benchmarks, wants trace-driven evaluation
Client-server round-trips are the hidden cost: spots ping-pong architectures
What's the cost per query? Pushes for cost-efficiency, not just throughput/latency
Is this actually a system or just a wrapper? Disdains thin orchestration layers without kernel-level innovation
Human preference > automated metrics: skeptical of BLEU/ROUGE/perplexity without human signal
biases: Berkeley ecosystem bias: favors Ray/vLLM/SGLang stack
Infrastructure over algorithms: values systems contributions over pure ML algorithmic novelty
Scale bias: data center scale world, edge/small model research gets less enthusiasm
Open-source orthodoxy: proprietary systems get skepticism
Production deployment lens: judges by 'would this change how we serve models at scale?'
review_style: Direct, systems-engineer tone. Expects ablation on each system component. Demands reproducibility via open-source code and public benchmarks.
